arxiv-2206-11794.title: A non-linear solution to the S 8 S_{8} tension?
arxiv-2206-11794.creator: Alexandra Amon, George Efstathiou 1 {1} Kavli Institute for Cosmology Cambridge, Madingley Road, Cambridge, CB3 OHA
arxiv-2206-11794.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Alexandra Amon, George Efstathiou 1 {1} Kavli Institute for Cosmology Cambridge, Madingley Road, Cambridge, CB3 OHA. Weak galaxy lensing surveys have consistently reported a lower amplitude for the matter fluctuation spectrum, as measured by the S 8 S_{8} parameter, than expected in the Λ ​ CDM \Lambda{\rm CDM} cosmology favoured by Planck . However, the expansion history follows the predictions of the Planck Λ ​ CDM \Lambda{\rm CDM} cosmology to high accuracy, as do measurements of lensing of the cosmic microwave background anisotropies.

arxiv-2304-03123.title: First-time sensitive homeomorphisms Thanks: 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification : Primary 37D10; Secondary 37B99.
arxiv-2304-03123.creator: Mayara Antunes and Bernardo Carvalho
arxiv-2304-03123.description: Abstract . We introduce first-time sensitivity for a homeomorphism of a compact metric space, that is a condition on the first increasing times of open balls of the space. Continuum-wise expansive homeomorphisms, the shift map on the Hilbert cube, and also some partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms satisfy this condition.

arxiv-2310-14340.title: Social Commonsense-Guided Search Query Generation for Open-Domain Knowledge-Powered Conversations
arxiv-2310-14340.creator: Revanth Gangi Reddy Hao Bai Wentao Yao Sharath Chandra Etagi Suresh
arxiv-2310-14340.description: Abstract Open-domain dialog involves generating search queries that help obtain relevant knowledge for holding informative conversations. However, it can be challenging to determine what information to retrieve when the user is passive and does not express a clear need or request.

arxiv-2401-02302.title: A survey on divisibility of ultrafilters Boris Šobot Department of Mathematics and Informatics, University of Novi Sad, Trg Dositeja Obradovića 4, 21000 Novi Sad, Serbia e-mail: sobot@dmi.uns.ac.rs ORCID: 0000-0002-4848-0678
arxiv-2401-02302.description: Abstract An extension of the divisibility relation on ℕ \mathbb{N} to the set β ​ ℕ \beta\mathbb{N} of ultrafilters on ℕ \mathbb{N} was defined and investigated in several papers during the last ten years. Here we make a survey of results obtained so far, adding several results connecting the themes of different stages of the research.

arxiv-2402-03225.title: The change of vertex energy when joining trees.
arxiv-2402-03225.creator: Octavio Arizmendi, Saylé Sigarreta
arxiv-2402-03225.description: Abstract In this manuscript we study how the vertex energy of a tree is affected when joined with a bipartite graph. We find an alternating pattern with respect to the coalescence vertex: the energy decreases for vertices located at odd distances and increases for those located at even distances. Keywords : graph energy, graph join, trees.

arxiv-2407-20577.title: Conductance of atomic size contacts of Ag and Au at high magnetic fields
arxiv-2407-20577.creator: Beilun Wu, Andrés Martínez, Paula Obladen, Marta Fernández-Lomana, Edwin Herrera, Carlos Sabater, Juan José Palacios, Isabel Guillamón, Hermann Suderow
arxiv-2407-20577.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Beilun Wu, Andrés Martínez, Paula Obladen, Marta Fernández-Lomana, Edwin Herrera, Carlos Sabater, Juan José Palacios, Isabel Guillamón, Hermann Suderow. Electronic conduction at the atomic scale can be described by Landauer’s formalism. In single atom point contacts of noble metals like Au and Ag, there is just one channel open between both electrodes and the conductance is very close to the quantum of conductance G ≈ G 0 = 2 ​ e 2 h G\approx G_{0}=\frac{2e^{2}}{h} , with the factor of two coming from spin

arxiv-2505-19646.title: Energy-based generator matching: A neural sampler for general state space
arxiv-2505-19646.creator: Dongyeop Woo, Minsu Kim, Minkyu Kim, Kiyoung Seong, Sungsoo Ahn
arxiv-2505-19646.description: Abstract We propose Energy-based generator matching (EGM) , a modality-agnostic approach to train generative models from energy functions in the absence of data. Extending the recently proposed generator matching, EGM enables training of arbitrary continuous-time Markov processes, e.g., diffusion, flow, and jump, and can generate data from continuous, discrete, and a mixture of two modalities.

arxiv-2601-07750.title: Central polynomials of minimal degree for matrices Thanks: The research of the second named author was supported by the National Programme of Ministry of Education and Science “Young Scientists and Post-Doctoral Researchers - 2”.
arxiv-2601-07750.creator: Vesselin Drensky, Boyan Kostadinov
arxiv-2601-07750.description: Abstract . Formanek made the conjecture that the minimal degree of the central polynomials for the n × n n\times n matrix algebra over a field of characteristic 0 is ( n 2 + 3 ​ n − 2 ) / 2 (n^{2}+3n-2)/2 and this is true for n ≤ 3 n\leq 3 .

arxiv-2602-12324.title: What Suppresses Star Formation in Bulge-Dominated Early-Type Galaxies?
arxiv-2602-12324.creator: Lori E. Porter, S. M. R. Jeffreson, Greg L. Bryan, Lars Hernquist
arxiv-2602-12324.description: Abstract We investigate the physical origin of star formation suppression in gas-rich early-type galaxies using five high-resolution hydrodynamical idealized galaxy simulations, performed with the moving-mesh code AREPO . These simulations include one Milky Way-like galaxy and four early-type galaxies, of which one early-type galaxy is found to have significantly less star formation despite a substantial molecular gas reservoir.

pmc-10736684.title: THE HEALTHY BRAIN INITIATIVE ROAD MAP CATALYZES ACTION AMONG STATE, LOCAL, AND NATIONAL PARTNERS
pmc-10736684.creator: Meghan Fadel, Peter Holtgrave, Carissa Beaty, Shelby Roberts
pmc-10736684.description: The Healthy Brain Initiative Road Map Series (Road Map) has achieved measurable success in spurring action in health departments across the country. Evaluation data from the Alzheimer’s Association shows all 50 states have implemented actions from the 2018-2023 Road Map and the majority of states completed at least one action in each of the four domains of the Road Map.

pmc-11460706.title: Effects of climate variability on the spatio-temporal distribution of Dengue in Valle del Cauca, Colombia, from 2001 to 2019
pmc-11460706.creator: Delia Ortega-Lenis, David Arango-Londoño, Freddy Hernández, Paula Moraga
pmc-11460706.description: Dengue is a vector-borne disease that has increased over the past two decades, becoming a global public health emergency. The transmission of dengue is contingent upon various factors, among which climate variability plays a significant role. However, there remains substantial uncertainty regarding the underlying mechanisms.

pmc-11631221.title: Public attitudes on performance for algorithmic and human decision-makers
pmc-11631221.creator: Kirk Bansak, Elisabeth Paulson
pmc-11631221.description: This study explores public preferences for algorithmic and human decision-makers (DMs) in high-stakes contexts, how these preferences are shaped by performance metrics, and whether public evaluations of performance differ depending on the type of DM. Leveraging a conjoint experimental design, approximately 9,000 respondents chose between pairs of DM profiles in two high-stakes scenarios: pretrial release decisions and bank loan approvals.

pmc-11639690.title: Transforming the Health Research Workforce in Mozambique: Achievements of the Mozambique Institute for Health Education and Research (MIHER) over a 13‑Year Journey
pmc-11639690.creator: Emília Virgínia Noormahomed, Sérgio Noormahomed, Matchecane Cossa, Nicole Joyce, Regina Daniel Miambo, Irina Mendes Sousa, Noémia Nhacupe, Tufária Mussá, Jahit Sacarlal, Lídia Gouveia, Luís Jorge Ferrão, Carla Carrilho, Mamudo Ismail, Davey Smith, Natasha K. Martin, Ravi Goyal, Kim E. Barrett, Sónia
pmc-11639690.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: African research capacity is challenged by insufficient infrastructure to solicit and manage grants from local and international funding agencies.Objective: The manuscript provides an overview and discusses lessons learned about the pioneering role of the Mozambique Institute for Health Education and Research (MIHER) as the first research support center (RSC) in supporting the management of research grants in Mozambique, emphasizing its impact on research capacity development.Methods: Using mixed methods, data were comprehensively collected to identify MIHER’s primary achievements from 2010 to 2023.

pmc-11644694.title: Nutrient Supplements for Young Children and Mothers’ Self Medication with Over-the-Counter Drugs During the COVID-19 Pandemic
pmc-11644694.creator: Esin Aydın Aksoy, Bahar Güçiz Doğan, Sıddıka Songül Yalçın, Pasquale Striano
pmc-11644694.description: Background: The restriction of access to health services during the COVID-19 pandemic has led to an increase in self-medication. This study aims to examine mothers’ use of nutrient supplements with over-the-counter (OTC) medications for their children, including instances of self-medication for themselves.

pmc-12502614.title: Interactions between LncRNAs and MAPK signaling pathways in the pathogenesis of breast cancer
pmc-12502614.creator: Baifang Ding, Xuguang Wang, Zhong Zhang, Yiwei Wang, Wei Bo, Mengyuan Zhang, Zitong Tian, Yaolu Wang, Xinyao Xue, Min Zhang
pmc-12502614.description: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) are increasingly recognized as key modulators of gene expression and cellular processes, playing pivotal roles in cancer biology. In breast cancer, a multifaceted malignancy driven by diverse genetic and epigenetic alterations, the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling pathway is critical for regulating processes such as cell proliferation, survival, and metastasis.

pmc-12574039.title: Artificial intelligence in cancer: applications, challenges, and future perspectives
pmc-12574039.creator: Cillian H. Cheng, Su-sheng Shi
pmc-12574039.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly revolutionizing the landscape of oncological research and the advancement of personalized clinical interventions. Progress in three interconnected areas, including the development of methods and algorithms for training AI models, the evolution of specialized computing hardware, and increased access to large volumes of cancer data such as imaging, genomics, and clinical information, has converged, leading to promising new applications of AI in cancer research.

pmc-12691097.title: Superparamagnetic Iron Oxide Used Alone Is Non-Inferior to the Combination of Radioactive Tracer and Superparamagnetic Iron Oxide in Detecting Sentinel Lymph Nodes in Early-Stage Vulvar Cancer
pmc-12691097.creator: Marcin A Jedryka, Tymoteusz Poprawski, Krzysztof Grobelak, Piotr Klimczak, Rafał Matkowski, Xavier Sastre-Garau
pmc-12691097.description: Simple SummarySentinel lymph node (SLN) detection is a recommended procedure for early-stage vulvar cancer, but the radioactive technique used as the standard of care has several drawbacks. Our goal was to determine whether an alternative, new method using superparamagnetic iron oxide (SPIO) as the sole tracer is effective and non-inferior to the standard technique.

pmc-12799450.title: Resolution Pharmacology: State-of-the-art and therapeutic landscape
pmc-12799450.creator: Mauro Perretti, Trinidad Montero-Melendez
pmc-12799450.description: In 2015, we coined the term “Resolution Pharmacology” to indicate how the biology of the resolution of inflammation could, and should, be harnessed to produce novel therapeutics. Here we update these concepts and discuss the most recent developments in this innovative field of pharmacology.

pmc-12844093.title: The Effect of Potentiostatic Control on the Bioreduction of Hexavalent Chromium Using Bacillus cereus
pmc-12844093.creator: Huimei Chi, Man Feng
pmc-12844093.description: Coupling microbial catalysis with electrochemical stimulation offers a promising strategy for heavy metal remediation. This study investigates how potentiostatic control influences the bioreduction of hexavalent chromium (Cr(VI)) by Bacillus cereus strain DIF1 in a bioelectrochemical system. Cr(VI) reduction was evaluated under various applied cathodic potentials, and the highest reduction efficiency (91.45%) was achieved at +0.04 V after 24 h.

pmc-13156614.title: Assessing the impacts of extreme precipitation on groundwater recharge under diverse hydrogeological conditions via the theis equation
pmc-13156614.creator: Qingtao Ma, Xinghang Zhang, Zhijie Bai, Sishan Pang, Guofei Shang, Zhaowang Chen, Ruohan Chen, Xiaoxia Hou, Yue Liu, Zhixian Wang, Shumin Han, Dandan Ren, Xiaojing Liu, Zhitong Ma
pmc-13156614.description: SummaryClimate change has amplified the frequency of extreme high-intensity precipitation events, altering groundwater recharge across diverse hydrogeological settings. Using observed precipitation, groundwater level (GL), hydrogeological drilling data, and the Theis equation, we quantified how precipitation affects groundwater in the Baiyangdian-Basin Plain. We found that GL declined in 80% of counties, with a milder decrease in piedmont regions.

pmc-13243631.title: Strain-enhanced stretchable molecular ferroelectric acoustic fibers
pmc-13243631.creator: Lei Liu, Shengxin Xiang, Qiongfeng Shi, Shengshun Duan, Xiao Wei, Gang Yu, Zhishui Chen, Huiyun Zhang, Jianlong Hong, Tong Zheng, Yu-an Xiong, Yu-Meng You, Jun Wu
pmc-13243631.description: Molecular ferroelectrics—hybrid organic-inorganic architectures that exhibit piezoelectric coefficients comparable to classic oxide ceramics while offering rich compositional and structural tunability—have emerged as promising materials for human-interfaced high-frequency acoustic sensing. Nevertheless, the inherent brittleness and relatively high modulus hinder their practical deployment on dynamically deformable interfaces.

pmc-13334933.title: Balancing Protection and Autonomy: Adolescent Sexual Rights and the Limits of Criminal Law in Kenya
pmc-13334933.creator: Mourice Onyango Okuon, Rita Babirye
pmc-13334933.description: onsensual, noncoercive, and non-exploitative sexual relations is constitutional. The petitioners argued that such prosecutions are discriminatory because they target boys as the perpetrators and girls as the victims. Their central argument, however, was that the impugned sections of the Sexual Offences Act (SOA) limited the rights of adolescents without meeting the proportionality and justification tests envisioned by the Kenyan Constitution.

pmc-13352757.title: Host-driven adaptive radiation and host usage in sponge-associated barnacles
pmc-13352757.creator: Meng-Chen Yu, Hsiu-Chin Lin, Gregory A Kolbasov, Jens T Høeg, Benny K K Chan
pmc-13352757.description: BackgroundAdaptive radiation often involves ecological and morphological diversification, influenced by environmental opportunities, such as symbiotic interactions. Sponge-associated barnacles have evolved specialized traits, such as modified shells, to thrive within sponge hosts. However, the evolutionary mechanisms driving their diversification and host specificity remain unclear.

pmc-13484492.title: A hybrid feature selection framework for dimensionality-optimized customer churn prediction
pmc-13484492.creator: Amina Saleh Omar, Kennedy Ogada, Kevin Tole
pmc-13484492.description: Customer churn is a major problem in the fiercely competitive telecom industry. It directly influences the profitability of a company and its future in the industry. There have already been successful applications of machine learning and deep learning (ML/DL) techniques to detect client churn. learning (ML/DL) techniques to detect client churn.

pmc-13653425.title: Resistance to disinfection emerges in Salmonella Typhimurium following cyclic exposure to 3-(diethylamino)propylamine
pmc-13653425.creator: Alberto Fau, Jorge Andaluz-Arbe, Francisco de Borja Sánchez-Melendo, Diego Gómez-Lozano, Rafael Pagán, Diego García-Gonzalo, Daniel Berdejo
pmc-13653425.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Highlights•Repeated lethal 3-(diethylamino)propylamine exposure selected tolerant variants.•Resistance outcomes varied among the three laboratory evolution protocols.•Obtained variants survived >1000-fold better after heat treatment.•Two obtained variants showed a two-fold increase in gentamicin MIC.•Resistance phenotypes varied according to the mutations identified.Keywords: Adaptive laboratory evolution, Disinfectant, Biocide, Resistant genetic variants, Thermotolerance, Antibiotic cross-resistance

Introduction

The European Union One Health 2024 Zoonoses report recorded > 1000 foodborne outbreaks related to Salmonella spp., with salmonellosis being the second most frequently reported food-borne gastrointestinal disease (EFSA and ECDC, 2025).

pmc-13654051.title: From classroom to clinic: Evaluating the educational utility of two Thiel embalming methods
pmc-13654051.creator: Veronica Antipova, Martin Siwetz, Simone Manhal, Niels Hammer
pmc-13654051.description: Over three decades since its introduction, the Thiel embalming method remains a widely used and praised technique in anatomical education and clinical training. This study compared for the first time the Thiel original protocol (TO) and a Modified version (TM) across user groups—undergraduate medical students, student demonstrators in anatomy, postgraduate trainees, and expert anatomists—to evaluate tissue quality and educational suitability.
